why: Reads the first field of that name at any depth, so a nested object's copy is reported as the profile's value. `configFor` resolves the profile's OWN field, so the sweep would then verify an untouched profile against a number the simulation never reads -- and pass. Today ai-profiles.json is flat, which is why the fixture carries the nested case deliberately: the guard has to fail now rather than on the day a profile gains a nested block.
killedBy: readProfileField: what the profiles a sweep leaves alone should still say reads the profile s OWN field, not a nested object s copy of it
